club: Maples Tech Club (MTC) — Learn it. Build it. Ship it.

questions.question_text: Which key on a Windows keyboard is used to capture a screenshot of your entire screen?
When a file or folder is selected on Windows, pressing which function key lets you RENAME it immediately?
What does pressing Alt + F4 do on a Windows computer?
questions.option_b: Closes the currently active app or window

questions.question_text: In a browser, pressing Ctrl and the "+" (plus) key together does what?
questions.option_d: Zooms in to make text and images appear larger

questions.question_text: After zooming in on a webpage, pressing Ctrl + 0 (zero) does what?
questions.option_b: Resets the page zoom back to normal (100%)

questions.question_text: When filling out an online form (like Name, Roll No, Class), pressing the Tab key usually does what?
questions.option_a: Moves the cursor neatly to the next input box

questions.question_text: If you step away from a computer for a minute, which Windows shortcut immediately LOCKS your screen?
Which Windows shortcut minimizes all open windows at once so you can see the Desktop?
You accidentally closed an important tab in Chrome/Edge! Which lifesaver shortcut reopens the last closed tab?
What happens when you delete a file using Shift + Delete instead of just pressing Delete?
questions.option_a: It moves the file to Desktop
questions.option_c: It permanently deletes the file without sending it to the Recycle Bin

questions.question_text: Which Windows shortcut opens File Explorer ("This PC" / Folders) directly?
While typing a sentence, holding Ctrl and pressing Backspace (Ctrl + Backspace) erases what?
questions.option_d: The entire word to the left of the cursor at once

questions.question_text: Which function key toggles Full-Screen mode ON or OFF in almost all web browsers?
If a program freezes on Windows, which direct shortcut opens Task Manager immediately?
Which modern Windows shortcut lets you drag and capture a screenshot of just ONE selected area of your screen?
In Word, Google Docs, or Notepad, which shortcut opens "Find and Replace" to swap a repeated word across the whole file?
In a web browser, pressing Ctrl + L (or Alt + D) quickly highlights what?
questions.option_a: The top Address / URL bar so you can type a website or search immediately
questions.option_d: The bottom footer of the webpage

questions.question_text: In Word, Google Docs, or email apps, pressing Ctrl + K on selected text lets you insert what?
Which newer oval-shaped reversible charging/data port is found on almost all modern Android phones and newer laptops?
What do we call the main circuit board inside a computer that connects the processor, RAM, storage, and ports together?
If a wireless mouse stops moving the cursor on screen, what is the FIRST simple hardware thing you should check?
questions.option_d: Check if its battery is low or its tiny power switch underneath is turned OFF

questions.question_text: A pen-like tool used by digital artists and students to write or draw neatly on a tablet screen is called a:
Which storage capacity is LARGER when comparing a pendrive or laptop storage?
Roughly how many Gigabytes (GB) make 1 Terabyte (TB) on a hard drive?
Before pulling out a USB pendrive while files are copying, why should you wait or click "Eject"?
questions.option_c: Pulling it out mid-write can corrupt or damage the files being saved
questions.option_d: Otherwise the monitor turns black forever

questions.question_text: Which computer component is specially helpful for smooth 3D video editing, animation, and modern games?
Why should you NEVER block the air vents on the bottom of a laptop by placing it deep into a thick blanket for hours?
questions.option_b: It makes the screen brightness drop to zero
questions.option_c: Blocked vents trap heat inside, causing overheating, slow performance, and battery wear

questions.question_text: A desktop monitor is turned ON, its power light is blinking, and it says "No Signal." What is the most likely practical cause?
questions.option_b: Either the CPU cabinet is OFF or the HDMI/VGA display cable between the CPU and monitor is loose
questions.option_d: Caps Lock is pressed on the keyboard

questions.question_text: What is the difference between putting a laptop to "Sleep" versus "Shut Down"?
questions.option_a: Sleep keeps open work ready in low-power memory for instant wake-up; Shut Down closes everything completely
questions.option_b: Shut Down uses more battery than playing games

questions.question_text: What does screen resolution like "1920 × 1080 (Full HD)" describe on a monitor or phone?
questions.option_a: The weight of the monitor in grams
questions.option_b: The grid of tiny pixels (width × height) that makes up the sharpness of the display
questions.option_c: How many files can fit on the desktop

questions.question_text: An "All-in-One" desktop PC in a modern lab has no separate tower box on the desk. Where are its processor, RAM, and SSD located?
questions.option_a: Built neatly right behind the monitor screen itself

questions.question_text: Why do ink-tank or laser printers usually cost much less per page for a school office than tiny cheap ink-cartridge printers?
questions.option_d: Refill ink bottles and toner print thousands of pages at a fraction of the cost per page

questions.question_text: What does a "60Hz" vs "120Hz" refresh rate on a phone or monitor screen mean in everyday use?
questions.option_b: How many apps can be installed
questions.option_c: How many hours the battery lasts
questions.option_d: How many times per second the screen updates the image — higher feels smoother while scrolling

questions.question_text: On headphones with a single 3.5mm plug (TRRS) used on laptops and phones, what does that single plug carry?
questions.option_d: Left audio, Right audio, AND Microphone voice signal together

questions.question_text: What is "Surge Protection" on a good computer extension spike-guard?
questions.option_a: A tool that blocks pop-up ads
questions.option_b: A feature that speeds up typing
questions.option_c: Protection that shields connected computers from sudden high-voltage electricity spikes

questions.question_text: If your phone says "Storage Almost Full (98% used)", which action frees up real internal storage space?
questions.option_b: Backing up large old videos/downloads to cloud or PC and deleting unneeded heavy files/apps

questions.question_text: On Windows, files ending in ".exe" (or ".apk" on Android) are what kind of files?
questions.option_c: Application installer / executable program files (only run from trusted official sources!)

questions.question_text: Before editing an important project presentation, why is naming files clearly like "Science_Poster_v2_Final.pptx" better than "asdf123.pptx"?
questions.option_a: Clear file names let you and your teammates find the right version in seconds without confusion
questions.option_d: Computers refuse to save short names

questions.question_text: What does the "Spell Check" wavy red underline in Word or Google Docs indicate?
questions.option_a: A word that may have a spelling typo so you can review and fix it
questions.option_b: That the computer has a virus
questions.option_c: That the sentence will be deleted automatically

questions.question_text: If a single app stops responding ("Not Responding") on Windows, how can you close JUST that stuck app without unplugging the whole PC?
questions.option_a: Pull the electric plug from the wall
questions.option_b: Open Task Manager, select the frozen app, and click "End Task"

questions.question_text: What is "Open-Source Software" (such as Linux, VLC, Blender, or LibreOffice)?
questions.option_a: Software that works only for 1 hour
questions.option_c: Software whose source code is openly shared so anyone can use, study, and improve it legally
questions.option_d: Software that leaves your computer unlocked to strangers

questions.question_text: When you install a new PDF app and Windows asks which "Default App" should open .pdf files, what does that setting control?
questions.option_d: Which program opens automatically whenever you double-click any .pdf file

questions.question_text: In Google Docs or Microsoft 365 Online, what is a huge everyday advantage of "Auto-Save" to the cloud?
questions.option_a: It writes your homework by itself
questions.option_b: It works without turning on the screen
questions.option_d: Your latest edits are saved continuously, so a sudden power cut does not wipe out an hour of typing

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of Windows Security / Antivirus software on a PC?
questions.option_b: To detect and block harmful malware or infected downloads before they damage your files
questions.option_c: To clean physical dust off the keyboard

questions.question_text: Why do phones and laptops let you turn off unnecessary "Startup Apps" in Settings?
questions.option_a: It turns off the screen color
questions.option_c: Fewer heavy apps launching automatically at boot makes the computer start up faster and saves memory

questions.question_text: When you download a `.zip` archive of club photos, why should you "Extract All" before editing the photos inside?
questions.option_a: Extracting unpacks the compressed files into a normal folder so apps can open and save changes properly
questions.option_d: Otherwise the photos turn black and white

questions.question_text: What does "Version History" in Google Docs, Slides, or Sheets let a student team do?
questions.option_a: See earlier saved versions of a document and restore work if someone accidentally erased a section
questions.option_b: See every website visited on the computer

questions.question_text: If you copy a song file onto your Desktop as a "Shortcut" (tiny arrow on the icon) and then copy ONLY that shortcut to a pendrive, what happens at school?
questions.option_b: It will NOT play, because a shortcut is only a pointer link — not the actual `.mp3` song file itself!
questions.option_c: It converts the song into a video

questions.question_text: What is a `.csv` (Comma-Separated Values) file commonly used for between apps like Excel, Google Sheets, and portals?
questions.option_c: Importing or exporting simple clean rows and columns of table data (like student lists or questions)

questions.question_text: On a phone or computer, what is the difference between "Clearing App Cache" and "Clearing App Data / Storage"?
questions.option_c: Clearing Cache deletes all your contacts
questions.option_d: Clearing Cache removes temporary files safely; Clearing Data resets the app like a fresh install and logs you out

questions.question_text: Why is "Restarting" a computer sometimes more helpful than "Shut Down and Turn On" when fixing a minor software glitch?
questions.option_d: Restart performs a clean full reload of the operating system and drivers from scratch

questions.question_text: What does "Cloud Sync" (like Google Drive, OneDrive, or Google Photos backup) protect you from?
questions.option_b: Losing your important school projects or photos if your phone or pendrive gets lost or damaged

questions.question_text: When printing a 20-page document and you only need Page 3 and Page 4, what should you choose in the Print dialog?
questions.option_b: Print all 20 pages and throw 18 away
questions.option_c: Select "Custom Pages" and type `3-4` so you do not waste 18 extra sheets of paper
questions.option_d: Delete the other 18 pages from your original file

questions.question_text: What does "Portrait" vs "Landscape" orientation mean when printing a certificate or poster?
questions.option_a: Portrait is tall/vertical (like a book page); Landscape is wide/horizontal (like a certificate)
questions.option_b: Portrait is color; Landscape is black-and-white
questions.option_d: Portrait prints only faces; Landscape prints only trees

questions.question_text: What is Google Drive or Microsoft OneDrive an example of?
questions.option_a: Cloud storage — lets you save files online and open or share them from any phone or computer
questions.option_d: A physical pendrive inside your pocket

questions.question_text: When sharing a Google Drive project link with your teacher, why should you check whether access is set to "Restricted" vs "Anyone with the link can View"?
questions.option_a: If left "Restricted", your teacher will see "Access Denied" when clicking your submitted link!
questions.option_c: View access lets anyone delete your account

questions.question_text: On a noisy browser tab playing unexpected music, what does the tiny speaker icon on that tab let you see or do?
questions.option_b: Spot immediately which tab is playing sound and even mute that tab

questions.question_text: What does an email ending in `.edu.in`, `.ac.in`, or `.gov.in` in India tell you about the website/sender?
questions.option_c: It belongs to a verified Indian educational institution (`.edu.in`/`.ac.in`) or government body (`.gov.in`)
questions.option_d: Anyone can buy it anonymously for ₹10 without verification

questions.question_text: If you start writing an email in Gmail and close the tab before clicking Send, where is your unfinished message saved automatically?
What is a "Browser Extension" (or Add-on)?
questions.option_d: A small optional helper tool added inside your browser (which you should install ONLY from trusted creators)

questions.question_text: If you want to save an online exam admit card or receipt neatly so you can view it offline anytime without internet, what can you select in the Print (`Ctrl + P`) destination menu?
When a random flashy website suddenly asks "Allow this site to send you Notifications?", what is the smart habit if you do not need alerts from it?
questions.option_b: Always click Allow on every site
questions.option_c: Click "Block" — allowing shady sites to send notifications floods your screen with fake virus/ad pop-ups!

questions.question_text: When sending an email announcement to 50 parents or students who do not know each other, why is `BCC` better than `CC`?
questions.option_a: `BCC` (Blind Carbon Copy) keeps everyone’s email address private from the other recipients

questions.question_text: In an email thread sent to 40 club members, what happens if you click "Reply All" instead of "Reply"?
questions.option_a: Your reply goes to ALL 40 people in the group instead of just the sender!

questions.question_text: Look closely at two URLs: `https://sbi.co.in` vs `https://sbi-login-kyc.freehost.xyz`. In the second URL, which company actually owns the real website domain?
questions.option_b: `freehost.xyz` — the `sbi-login-kyc` part at the front is just a fake subdomain trick!

questions.question_text: If a webpage looks broken or keeps showing an outdated version even after refreshing, what browser step usually fixes it?
questions.option_c: Hard Refresh (`Ctrl + F5`) or clearing cached images and files for that site

questions.question_text: In Chrome/Edge, why is creating separate "Browser Profiles" helpful when two siblings share one home laptop?
questions.option_c: It doubles the laptop hard disk size
questions.option_d: Each sibling gets their own separate bookmarks, history, and logged-in school accounts without mixing them up

questions.question_text: Why shouldn’t you blindly trust a shortened mystery link (like `bit.ly/3xYz99`) sent by an unknown stranger?
questions.option_a: Short links only work on desktop PCs
questions.option_b: Short links use 10 GB of data
questions.option_d: Shortened links hide the real destination website URL until clicked, so they can disguise phishing or scam sites

questions.question_text: When sharing a Google Doc with a teammate, what is the difference between giving "Commenter" access vs "Editor" access?
questions.option_b: A Commenter can suggest notes without changing your original text; an Editor can directly change or delete content
questions.option_c: A Commenter cannot even read the document

questions.question_text: Why do most email services (like Gmail) stop direct attachments larger than 25 MB, and how do you send a 200 MB project video cleanly?
questions.option_a: Videos can never be shared online
questions.option_b: Cut the video into 200 separate 1-second emails
questions.option_c: Email inboxes aren’t built for huge files — upload the video to Google Drive/OneDrive and share its link instead
questions.option_d: Rename `.mp4` to `.txt` so it shrinks to zero

questions.question_text: What does "Pinning a Tab" (Right-click tab → Pin) do in Chrome, Edge, or Firefox?
questions.option_a: Shrinks the tab neatly to the far left without a close (✕) button so you don’t close it by accident
questions.option_b: Sends the tab to your friends
questions.option_c: Downloads every image on the page

questions.question_text: When you hover your mouse over a button or link (without clicking yet), where does the browser preview the real destination URL?
questions.option_a: In the bottom-left corner of the browser window

questions.question_text: On a laptop connected to someone’s mobile Hotspot, turning ON "Metered Connection" (or Data Saver) helps because:
questions.option_a: It pauses huge background Windows updates so your friend’s mobile data does not drain suddenly

questions.question_text: On modern dual-band home Wi-Fi routers, you often see two Wi-Fi names: `Home_2.4G` and `Home_5G`. What is the practical difference?
questions.option_a: `5G` Wi-Fi requires a 5G SIM card inside the router
questions.option_b: `5 GHz` gives faster speeds nearby in the same room; `2.4 GHz` reaches farther through walls
questions.option_c: There is no difference at all

questions.question_text: What is "Quick Share / Nearby Share / AirDrop" on modern phones and laptops used for?
questions.option_c: Sending photos or project files fast between two nearby devices wirelessly without wasting internet data
questions.option_d: Charging another phone from 10 meters away

questions.question_text: Why should you avoid logging into banking or sensitive accounts on an open, password-free public Wi-Fi at a railway station or café?
questions.option_b: Public Wi-Fi breaks your phone camera
questions.option_d: Unsecured open Wi-Fi networks make it easier for attackers nearby to snoop on traffic or set up fake twin hotspots

questions.question_text: In online video calls or multiplayer games, what does "High Ping / High Latency" (e.g., 450 ms instead of 25 ms) feel like?
questions.option_d: A noticeable delay or lag between clicking/speaking and getting a response back

questions.question_text: What brings ultrahigh-speed broadband into modern schools and homes using hair-thin strands of glass carrying pulses of light?
If the home internet suddenly stops working on ALL phones and laptops at once, what safe 1-minute step often resolves a stuck router?
questions.option_b: Factory-reset every phone in the house
questions.option_c: Power-cycle the router: turn it OFF, wait 15–30 seconds, and turn it back ON

questions.question_text: What does "NFC" (Near Field Communication) on modern phones and smart cards allow?
questions.option_a: Tap-to-pay or instant pairing when held within a few centimeters of a reader/tag

questions.question_text: When you type `mapleskhatauli.com` in your browser, which behind-the-scenes internet phonebook translates that friendly name into the server’s numeric IP address?
Your internet speed test shows `100 Mbps` (Megabits per second). Since 8 bits = 1 Byte, roughly how many Megabytes (`MB`) can download in 1 second?
Why is setting up a separate "Guest Wi-Fi" network on a home or school router a smart security practice for visitors?
questions.option_a: Guest Wi-Fi doubles your ISP plan speed
questions.option_c: Visitors get internet access while keeping your main school/home computers and shared printers isolated and private

questions.question_text: What is "USB Tethering" between a smartphone and a desktop PC that has no Wi-Fi adapter?
questions.option_b: Printing photos directly from SIM card
questions.option_c: Tying the phone to the desk with a rope
questions.option_d: Sharing your phone’s internet connection directly to the desktop PC through a normal USB charging/data cable!

questions.question_text: What is the role of a "Firewall" in Windows or a school router?
questions.option_a: It prevents physical fire in the computer room
questions.option_b: It heats up the CPU in winter
questions.option_d: It monitors incoming and outgoing network traffic and blocks unauthorized outside connections

questions.question_text: Why should you change the default admin login (`admin / admin`) printed on the bottom sticker of a new home Wi-Fi router?
questions.option_b: Anyone connected nearby who knows common default logins could open router settings and change your Wi-Fi or DNS!
questions.option_c: Otherwise Wi-Fi turns off after 24 hours

questions.question_text: When setting a Wi-Fi security type on a modern router, why should you pick `WPA2` or `WPA3` instead of `"Open"` or old `"WEP"`?
questions.option_a: Security settings only change router LED color
questions.option_c: `WPA2` / `WPA3` strongly encrypt your wireless Wi-Fi traffic, whereas Open/WEP are insecure
questions.option_d: `WPA3` blocks your own laptop from connecting

questions.question_text: During a live Zoom/Google Meet class on weak internet, turning OFF your own HD video feed when not speaking helps audio stay clear because:
questions.option_a: Live video uses much more bandwidth than voice, so pausing video leaves enough bandwidth for smooth audio
questions.option_b: Microphones stop working when cameras are on
questions.option_c: Audio does not use the internet

questions.question_text: What is the difference between a Modem (ONT) and a Wi-Fi Router (often combined into one box today)?
questions.option_a: The Modem connects to the ISP’s outside fiber/cable line; the Router shares that internet across all your home devices
questions.option_b: The Modem prints paper; the Router scans paper
questions.option_c: The Router works without a Modem or ISP line
questions.option_d: Modems are only for Bluetooth earbuds

questions.question_text: Where is the single best place in a house to keep a Wi-Fi router for even signal coverage across rooms?
questions.option_a: Locked inside a thick steel almirah
questions.option_b: In a central, open, slightly elevated spot — NOT hidden inside a closed metal cupboard or corner floor
questions.option_d: Directly behind a microwave oven on the floor

questions.question_text: Why do phones and Windows regularly release "Security Updates"?
questions.option_b: To patch newly discovered security holes so hackers and malware cannot exploit them

questions.question_text: If a classmate accidentally left their Gmail open on a school lab computer, what is the ONLY ethical thing to do?
questions.option_a: Send a prank email from their account
questions.option_c: Immediately click "Sign Out" without reading a single email, and politely let them know to be careful next time
questions.option_d: Read their private emails for fun

questions.question_text: Sometimes AI chatbots confidently make up a fake book title, date, or fact that sounds very believable. What should you do before putting AI facts into a school project?
questions.option_c: Assume computers can never be wrong
questions.option_d: Verify important facts, dates, and quotes from a reliable textbook or trusted official website

questions.question_text: Why is keeping phones on silent and putting screens away at least 30–45 minutes before sleep recommended by doctors?
questions.option_d: Bright late-night screens and endless notifications disturb deep sleep and leave you tired in class the next morning

questions.question_text: If you receive an uncomfortable, threatening, or scam message from an unknown account online, what 3 steps protect you best?
questions.option_b: Do NOT reply or argue — take a screenshot as proof if needed, Block/Report the account, and tell a trusted parent or teacher
questions.option_c: Send them your phone number to argue back
questions.option_d: Keep it secret and worry alone

questions.question_text: What is "Plagiarism" in school projects and digital work?
questions.option_b: Saving a backup copy on a pendrive
questions.option_c: Copying someone else’s article, code, or artwork and presenting it as your own original work without credit

questions.question_text: When sitting at a computer desk for an hour, what healthy posture avoids neck and back ache?
questions.option_a: Sit upright with feet flat, shoulders relaxed, and top of the screen near eye level rather than hunching low
questions.option_c: Keep the monitor on the floor
questions.option_d: Bend your neck 90 degrees inches from the keyboard

questions.question_text: What is India’s official national Cyber Crime Helpline number (and portal `cybercrime.gov.in`) in case a family member faces online financial fraud?
What is a "Deepfake" video or voice clip that everyone on social media needs to be aware of today?
questions.option_b: An AI-manipulated video or cloned voice that makes a real person appear to say or do something they NEVER actually did
questions.option_d: A backup stored deep inside a folder

questions.question_text: Someone calls your parent in panic using a realistic-sounding voice saying "Send ₹10,000 urgently to this new number, don’t tell anyone!" What is the smart verification habit?
questions.option_a: Share bank OTPs on the call
questions.option_b: Install a screen-sharing app they suggest
questions.option_c: Pause, hang up, and call the family member directly on their REAL known phone number to verify before sending a rupee!
questions.option_d: Transfer money within 10 seconds in panic

questions.question_text: Why do scammers urgently ask victims to install remote screen-sharing apps (like AnyDesk / TeamViewer / unknown `.apk`s) during fake "KYC / customer care" calls?
questions.option_a: Banks require AnyDesk for every account
questions.option_b: To double your mobile battery life
questions.option_c: To clean dust from your phone speaker
questions.option_d: Because screen-sharing lets the scammer see your live phone screen, including incoming bank OTPs and apps!

questions.question_text: When designing a club registration form (Data Minimization principle), which information is ethical and sensible to collect?
questions.option_a: Parents’ bank account numbers and Aadhaar passwords
questions.option_b: Home Wi-Fi passwords of every student
questions.option_d: Only what is genuinely needed for the club (Name, Roll No, Class, Section) — never unnecessary private family/financial data!

questions.question_text: What does a "Creative Commons (CC)" license on an online photo or music track tell students making a video project?
questions.option_a: Nobody is allowed to view the image
questions.option_b: The creator has given clear permission to reuse the work under stated conditions (such as giving proper attribution/credit)
questions.option_d: You can sell it as your own painting without credit

questions.question_text: What should families do with old dead batteries, broken chargers, and discarded electronics ("E-Waste") instead of burning them or tossing them in open drains?
questions.option_a: Break screens with a hammer in class
questions.option_b: Burn plastic circuit boards in the backyard
questions.option_c: Hand them over to authorized E-Waste collection/recycling centers so toxic metals don’t pollute soil and water

questions.question_text: Why do social media "recommendation algorithms" create an "Echo Chamber" if you are not mindful?
questions.option_a: They keep showing more of whatever you clicked before, which can make one-sided opinions or rumors look like the whole truth
questions.option_b: They delete posts older than 1 hour
questions.option_c: They turn off Wi-Fi in closed rooms
questions.option_d: They make your phone speaker echo loudly

questions.question_text: Before posting a close-up photo of your house keys, boarding pass barcode, or school exam admit card barcode publicly on Instagram/status, why should you pause?
questions.option_a: Visible QR codes, barcodes, roll/application IDs, and personal details in photos can be scanned and misused by strangers!
questions.option_d: There is no privacy risk at all

questions.question_text: What is "Ransomware", and what single everyday habit best protects your school/home projects against it?
questions.option_a: A free antivirus tool from Microsoft
questions.option_b: Malware that locks files and demands money — keeping regular offline/cloud backups and avoiding shady downloads protects you!

questions.question_text: What does true "Accessibility" mean when students build a website or poster for the school community?
questions.option_b: Locking the site so nobody can open it
questions.option_c: Using clear readable fonts, strong color contrast, and image descriptions (`alt` text) so everyone — including people with low vision — can use it comfortably
questions.option_d: Using tiny light-yellow text on a white background
